text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.
- President Franjo Tudjman is in extraordinarily good health and his medical treatment is about to be successfully completed, says his medical team.

- Trust in Croatian banks has returned and people are more willing to entrust them with their money. According to central bank figures, all banks recorded an increase in both kuna and foreign currency deposits in 1996.
- Production of gas is inadequate because current prices are too low and because Croatia has only limited resources.

- Prima Osiguranje, controlled by Austrian insurer Grazer Wechselseitige Versicherung AG, had some 71.4 million kuna (20 million marks) premium income in 1996. It says income will rise to more than 100 million kuna this year.
- Economic malpractice accounted for 16.85 percent of total criminal acts last year, up from 6.1 percent in 1993.
- Some 50 percent of Croatians will spend their summer holidays at home. Of those who can afford to travel, 86.7 percent will go to the Adriatic coast, according to research.

- Rise in unemployment is due to many factors including ending government employment policies because of a lack of funds. In 1996 Croatian firms estimated they had a surplus of 21,000 workers and the number of job vacancies dropped 2.9 percent compared to 1995.

- It is not realistic to expect the government to subsidise gas production in Dalmatia, says Zeljko Lalic, assistant minister of economy for energy. This is more likely to be a job of foreign or local subcontractors. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
